newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid sees digital imaging profit by '98.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid sees digital imaging profit by '98.

text.p: Polaroid Corp's digital imaging business will be profitable by 1998, a Polaroid spokesman told Reuters.
The company reduced the loss at the unit by $60 million in 1996, the spokesman, Robert Guenther, said. He added that a year ago, the unit had a loss of $180 million.
The unit contributes "less than 10 percent" of Polaroid's $2.28 billion in 1996 revenue, he also said.
He did not say what the existing loss was at the business or how much Polaroid had invested to grow the business.

In a press statement that accompanied the company's fourth-quarter and full-year earnings, Polaroid chairman Gary DiCamillo said that, "In the coming year, we will bring our digital imaging business closer to profitability."
Polaroid said Wednesday it earned $0.25 per share for the fourth quarter compared with a loss of $2.44 in the year-ago period.
